summary: A maiden gets married on Wednesday and a widow on Thursday. This is because the batei din sat on Mondays and Thursdays, so a chasan with a complaint could go to beis din right away.

chunks.en: A maiden gets married on Wednesday,
chunks.st: A virgin is married on Wednesday

words.note: A girl who was never married before.

chunks.en: and a widow on Thursday.
chunks.st: and a widow on Thursday.

chunks.he: שֶׁפַּעֲמַיִם בַּשַּׁבָּת בָּתֵּי דִינִין יוֹשְׁבִין בָּעֲיָרוֹת,
chunks.en: Because twice a week the batei din sit in the towns,
chunks.st: The reason for the former is that twice a week courts convene in the towns,

chunks.en: on Monday and on Thursday.
chunks.st: on Monday and Thursday,

chunks.en: So if the chasan has a complaint that she was not really a maiden,
chunks.st: so that if the husband had a claim concerning the bride’s virginity
chunks.stMore: when consummating the marriage on Wednesday night,

chunks.en: he can go early the next morning to the beis din.
chunks.st: he would go early the next day to court and make his claim.

summary: A maiden's kesubah is two hundred zuz, and a widow's is one hundred. A woman whose first marriage ended before the chuppah, or who became Jewish or was freed while very little, still counts as a maiden.

chunks.en: A maiden's kesubah is two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: a virgin, her marriage contract is two hundred dinars,

words.note: The marriage contract: money promised to the wife if the marriage ends.

chunks.en: and a widow's is one hundred.
chunks.st: and with regard to a widow, her marriage contract is one hundred dinars.

chunks.en: A maiden who became a widow,
chunks.st: With regard to a virgin who is a widow,

chunks.en: or was divorced, or had chalitzah,
chunks.st: a divorcée, or a ḥalutza

words.note: A widow freed by chalitzah from marrying her husband's brother.

chunks.en: after only the erusin,
chunks.st: who achieved that status from a state of betrothal,
chunks.stMore: before marriage and before consummation of the marriage,

words.note: The first step of marriage, before the chuppah.

chunks.en: their kesubah is two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: for all of these their marriage contract is two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and the husband can complain if she was not a maiden.
chunks.st: and they are subject to a claim concerning their virginity,
chunks.stMore: as their presumptive status of virginity is intact.

chunks.en: A woman who became a giyores, or a captive woman,
chunks.st: With regard to a female convert, or a captive woman,

chunks.en: or a maidservant, who were ransomed or became Jewish
chunks.st: or a maidservant, who were ransomed with regard to the captive, or who converted with regard to the convert,

chunks.he: וְשֶׁנִּשְׁתַּחְרְרוּ, פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: or were set free when they were younger than three years and one day,
chunks.st: or who were freed with regard to the maidservant, when they were less than three years and one day old,

chunks.en: their kesubah is two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: their marriage contract is two hundred
chunks.stMore: dinars, as their presumptive status is that of a virgin. Even if they were subject to intercourse when they were younger than that age, the hymen remains intact.

chunks.en: and the husband can complain if she was not a maiden.
chunks.st: And they are subject to a claim concerning their virginity.

summary: Rabbi Meir says that a girl who was hurt in certain ways still counts as a maiden, with a kesubah of two hundred. The Sages say a girl hurt by a piece of wood gets only one hundred.

chunks.en: A little girl who was harmed by a grown man,
chunks.st: an adult man who engaged in intercourse with a minor girl less than three years old;

chunks.en: or a grown woman who was with a young boy,
chunks.st: or a minor boy less than nine years old who engaged in intercourse with an adult woman;

chunks.en: or a girl who was hurt by a piece of wood,
chunks.explain: An accident made her no longer seem like a maiden.
chunks.st: or a woman who had her hymen ruptured by wood or any other foreign object,

chunks.en: their kesubah is two hundred zuz.
chunks.st: for all these women their marriage contract is two hundred
chunks.stMore: dinars, as their legal status is that of a virgin.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: a girl hurt by a piece of wood gets a kesubah of one hundred.
chunks.st: The marriage contract of a woman whose hymen was ruptured by wood is one hundred dinars,
chunks.stMore: as physically, since her hymen is not intact, she is no longer a virgin.

summary: A woman who was a widow or divorced after a full marriage gets a kesubah of one hundred, even if she is really still a maiden. The same is true for a giyores, captive or freed maidservant who was older than three.

chunks.en: A maiden who became a widow,
chunks.st: a virgin who is either a widow,

chunks.en: or was divorced, or had chalitzah,
chunks.st: a divorcée, or a ḥalutza

chunks.en: after a full marriage (the chuppah),
chunks.st: who achieved that status from a state of marriage,

chunks.en: her kesubah is one hundred,
chunks.st: for all these women their marriage contract is one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and the husband cannot complain that she was not a maiden.
chunks.st: and they are not subject to a claim concerning their virginity.
chunks.stMore: Since they were married, even if they did not engage in intercourse with their husband, their presumptive status is that of non-virgins, and the second husband cannot claim that he was misled with regard to their status as virgins.

chunks.en: A giyores, or a captive woman,

chunks.en: when they were older than three years and one day,
chunks.st: when they were more than three years and one day old,

chunks.en: their kesubah is one hundred,

chunks.en: and the husband cannot complain that she was not a maiden.
chunks.st: and they are not subject to a claim concerning their virginity.
chunks.stMore: When they married, their presumptive status was that of a non-virgin.

summary: In Yehudah a chasan could be alone with his kallah before the wedding, so he cannot complain later. The mishnah also teaches about a Kohen's daughter's kesubah.

chunks.he: הָאוֹכֵל אֵצֶל חָמִיו בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁלֹּא בְעֵדִים,

chunks.en: cannot complain that she was not a maiden,
chunks.st: is unable to make a claim concerning virginity after marriage

chunks.en: because he was alone with her.
chunks.st: because in accordance with the custom in Judea, the assumption is that he secluded himself with her,
chunks.stMore: and the concern is that it was he who engaged in intercourse with her.

chunks.he: אַחַת אַלְמְנַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַחַת אַלְמְנַת כֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: Both a regular widow and a Kohen's widow
chunks.st: For both a widow who is an Israelite woman and a widow who is the daughter of priests,

chunks.en: have a kesubah of one hundred.
chunks.st: her marriage contract is one hundred dinars.
